key_insight: LongE2V shows that a pre-trained video diffusion model can be adapted to event streams to produce sharper, more stable long-horizon video reconstruction and prediction than traditional regression-based methods. It unifies reconstruction, prediction, and frame interpolation in one generative framework.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of recovering high-quality video from sparse event data, especially over long time horizons where existing methods tend to blur details or drift in stability.
method: Fine-tunes a foundational video diffusion model to use event streams as conditioning input.
Jointly supports event-based video reconstruction, future frame prediction, and frame interpolation in a single model.
Improves data efficiency and perceptual quality by leveraging strong pre-trained diffusion priors instead of training from scratch.
impact: This matters because it offers a practical path to high-quality event-based video synthesis without requiring massive task-specific training data. For practitioners, it suggests diffusion priors can make sparse-sensing video systems more accurate, sharper, and more versatile.

paper_title: LongE2V: Long-Horizon Event-based Video Reconstruction, Prediction, and Frame Interpolation with Video Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Cheng-De Fan, Chun-Wei Tuan Mu, Chen-Wei Chang, Chin-Yang Lin, Kun-Ru Wu
